meta.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 · Materials science · community · run 1
meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 3 of 11 credited claims; 3 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

agents.brief: Work on /lab/data/expt_is_metal (binary classification, target 0/1, metric: error rate on held-out). Use the Magpie-style featurizer in the founder's gap/run.py as a starting point (parse_formula, feat_row with full elements.csv columns, stoichiometry p-norms, element fractions). Compare against the baseline in /lab/data/baselines/materials_baseline.py (run with: python materials_baseline.py expt_is_metal, 5-fold KFold(5, shuffle, rs=0), error rate). Any claim must come from lab exec runs. Use the prediction profile; write OUT_DIR/predictions.csv when EVAL_DIR is set. Post results on the board with lab post.

Work on /lab/data/glass (binary classification, glass-forming ability, target 0/1). Start from the founder's Magpie-style featurizer (blob from lab put on gap/run.py; feat_row + parse_formula). Try ExtraTrees and gradient boosting classifiers with class-weight/threshold tuning; compare against materials_baseline.py on the same 5-fold protocol. Evidence via lab exec only. Use the prediction profile and write predictions.csv for EVAL_DIR inputs. Report on the board.

Work on /lab/data/steels (regression, yield strength in MPa, only 240 training rows, 72 hidden). Start from the founder's featurizer (gap/run.py). Small data: try ExtraTrees, kernel ridge / GP on standardized features, and ensembles. Compare against materials_baseline.py (python materials_baseline.py steels) on the same 5-fold protocol. Evidence via lab exec only. Use the prediction profile. Report on the board.

claim.statement: Under the same 5-fold protocol, ExtraTrees with stock sklearn settings (sqrt features, no class weight) does not reliably beat materials_baseline.py: seed 0 0.1149 vs 0.1168 (diff -0.0019), seed 1 0.1208 vs 0.1196 (diff +0.0012). ExtraTrees with max_features=0.5 and no class weight gives 0.1128 (seed 0) and 0.1149 (seed 1), which beats the baseline on both seeds. Adding balanced weights to sqrt features does not help (0.1161, 0.1215). The published finding findin-facdafc0 used max_features=0.5 with balanced weights, a configuration I chose before the seed comparisons but did not test in isolation. Its advantage over the baseline is therefore real only for that configuration on the public rows, and the stock-settings result is not an improvement. The founder's default ET setting did not show the effect.

claim.statement: Descriptive 5-fold grid (KFold shuffle seeds 0 and 1, same 4230 rows, same features as the published finding, 300 trees, threshold 0.5), exec-b22ac613. Baseline CV error: 0.1168 (seed 0), 0.1196 (seed 1). ExtraTrees with max_features in {0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0}, with or without balanced weights, beats the baseline on both seeds (range 0.1111-0.1142 on seed 0; 0.1130-0.1170 on seed 1). The sqrt default fails on seed 1 (0.1225 without weights, 0.1222 balanced). The best cell on seed 0 is max_features 0.5 balanced (0.1111); on seed 1 the best is max_features 1.0 without weights (0.1130), so the published configuration is not uniquely best. Because these are the same rows used to choose the configuration, the margins are optimistic; the plateau is the more reliable part of the result.

events.text: I need to learn the lab's conventions before deciding on a research direction, so I'll read the guide, the command list, and the data READMEs first.
Before choosing a direction I need the baseline's details (it sets the bar), the contribution schema, and the truncated part of the guide.

I'll focus on `expt_gap` regression, since it has the most data and a clear error metric. First I need the rest of the baseline (metric, CV protocol) and a check that the libraries I need are installed.

The baseline is Magpie-lite features with HistGradientBoosting and a 5-fold MAE of about 0.3 eV on train. I'll write a richer featurizer (the full Magpie property set, weighted deviations, p-norms, element fractions) and compare three models: squared-loss HGB, L1-loss HGB, and ExtraTrees, plus their ensembles. Model selection uses the baseline's exact CV protocol, and I'll run the baseline itself for a same-session comparison.

The ExtraTrees configuration gets 0.423 eV CV MAE against the baseline's 0.471 under the same protocol, about 10% better. Before publishing, I'll check that the prediction path writes a valid `predictions.csv` on a mock held-out split.
